# Helping your midwife find you

### A little planning now can make a big difference when baby is on the way

Welcome to your home birth journey! We’re the Riverside community midwives, and we’re looking forward to caring for you and your family.

In the Philippines, we say that a midwife is like family. That’s how we hope you’ll feel about us: a friendly face coming to support you at an important moment.

There’s just one small thing: first, we need to find you! At 3am, even a street we know can look very different in the dark. A little preparation can help us get to your door and bring our equipment inside more easily.

## When to call us

**Phone the Riverside birth line when you think labour has started.** The birth line will put you in touch with the midwife who is on call.

Please use the birth line rather than your midwife’s personal mobile, even if you know her well. She may not be the midwife on call when your baby decides it’s time to make an appearance!

Home birth cover starts from **37 weeks of pregnancy**. If you think you are in labour before 37 weeks, you will need to go to hospital. Please phone the Riverside birth line for advice.

You can write the birth line number here and save it in your phone:

**Riverside birth line: __________________________________**

When you call, it helps to have your address ready, including your postcode and any instructions that will help us find and get into your home. You can also tell us about parking, permits or anything else you think we should know.

## Help us spot your home

You know exactly which home is yours, but it isn’t always obvious to someone arriving in the dark.

Please check that your house number or name can be seen clearly from the road. If you live in a named house, tell us the name **and** describe where it is. For example, you might tell us the colour of the door or which houses are next to it.

I once went looking for Rosemary Cottage in a street of terraces. The sat nav sent me to a chippy. Lovely as a chippy can be, it wasn’t where the baby was!

If you have an outside light, please switch it on when you call us at night. In winter, a porch light can be a midwife’s best friend.

Some families like to put something easy to spot on the gate or door. One family used balloons, and I found them straight away. You don’t need to throw us a party, but we do appreciate the directions!

## If you live in a flat

Flats and buildings don’t always follow the numbering we expect. I once spent 20 minutes going round a block in Everton because flat 14 wasn’t near flat 13 at all: it was in another building. In the end, Dad waved a tea towel from the window!

When you call, please tell us:

- The name or number of your building, and which entrance to use.
- Your flat number and floor.
- How to get through any main door, gate or intercom.
- Anything unusual about the numbering or layout.
- Whether there is a lift, and how to find it.

If someone can safely meet us at the entrance or wave from a window, that can be helpful too.

## Pins and what3words

If it would help us find your home, you can give us a **what3words** location or send a location pin by WhatsApp to the birth line phone.

Please still give us your address and any useful directions when you call. A pin can show us where to go, but it may not tell us which entrance to use or how to get through the door!

## A space for the midwives

Two midwives come for the birth, and we usually arrive in separate cars. If possible, please leave **two parking spaces** close to your home.

We may have quite a bit to carry, including gas and air cylinders, a big bag and sometimes equipment for a birthing pool. A nearby space saves our arms a little work before we’ve even reached your door!

There are permit parking zones around Anfield and Kensington. If a permit is needed where you live, please ask the council about a visitor permit and have it ready for us. If you already have a permit, you can leave it ready on the dashboard. We’ve had tickets before, and we’d much rather spend our time with you than worrying about parking.

If parking near your home is difficult, don’t worry. Just let us know when you call so we can plan where to go.

## Getting inside safely

Please make sure we can reach the right door and get in when we arrive. Let us know if there is a gate, shared entrance, intercom or anything else we need to know about.

I once walked into the wrong house because the door was open. Thankfully, a very nice gentleman offered me a Jammie Dodger! Clear directions will help us make sure we come to *your* home.

If you can, clear a path through the hallway and up the stairs before we arrive. Shoes, washing baskets and toys can all become unexpected obstacles when we’re carrying equipment. Lego is especially good at finding bare feet—and possibly midwives’ feet too.

Your home doesn’t need to be spotless. We’re coming to care for you, not to inspect your housekeeping. We just need enough clear space to get to you safely.

## A little help with pets

We know pets are part of the family too. I still remember Pippin the staffie, who loved me so much that he jumped up at every visit. On one occasion I nearly dropped the Entonox!

Please put pets safely in another room before we arrive, if you can. That gives us space to bring in our equipment and care for you, and it gives your pet somewhere calm to settle. They can come and meet the new arrival later.

## One last thing

Please don’t worry if your home is hard to find or parking is tricky. Every home is different, and we’re happy to help you work out a plan. Have a chat with your midwife during pregnancy, and remind the birth line when you call.

We’re looking forward to meeting your baby—and finding the right front door!

---

# Fridge checklist

**My Riverside birth line number: ______________________________**

### Before baby arrives

☐ I have saved the Riverside birth line number in my phone.

☐ I know home birth cover starts from **37 weeks**. Before then, I need to go to hospital if I think I’m in labour and phone the birth line for advice.

☐ My address, postcode and any helpful directions are easy to find.

☐ My house number or name can be seen, or I have a clear description to give the midwife.

☐ If I live in a flat, I know how to explain which building and entrance to use.

☐ I have thought about where two midwives could park, and a visitor permit if needed.

☐ I have a plan for putting pets safely in another room.

### When I think labour has started

☐ Phone the **Riverside birth line**, not my midwife’s personal mobile.

☐ Give my address, postcode and any instructions for finding and entering my home.

☐ Mention parking or permits, and send a pin or give what3words if helpful.

☐ Switch on the outside light if it’s dark.

☐ Clear a path through the hallway and stairs, if possible.

☐ Put pets safely in another room, if possible.

☐ Put the kettle on if there’s time. Just kidding—let’s find you first!
